DayBands.description:
How the day's published items split across the confidence bands.

Additive. Every published item carries exactly one band, so the three counts
partition the published set and a window's band counts are the daily counts
added up.

high.description: Items the checker did not doubt.
high.title: High

DayBands.title: DayBands

DayDistribution.description:
One numeric instrument aggregated over the day, split by how it combines.

`count` and `total` are additive: sum both over a window and divide once for
the window's mean, which is a mean over items and never a mean of daily
means. The quartiles and the range are the day's own and are NOT additive - a
reader shows a daily quartile or recomputes an exact one from a value
population this record does not carry. A day that measured nothing carries the
count 0, the total 0.0 and no order statistic; empty is not zero.

count.description: Items that carried a value. Additive.
count.title: Count

maximum.description: The day's largest value. Not additive.
maximum.title: Maximum

minimum.description: The day's smallest value. Not additive.
minimum.title: Minimum

p25.description: The day's lower quartile. Not additive.
p25.title: P25

p75.description: The day's upper quartile. Not additive.
p75.title: P75

DayDistribution.title: DayDistribution

DayExtraction.description:
What the candidate pass found on the day, and what the page drew from it.

Every count is additive across days, so a window is a sum and never a re-walk.
The two rates a reader wants are not stored, because a rate is not additive:
`idhazh.evals.metrics` derives both from these counts, and the console does
the same arithmetic on the same cells.

**Three classes and not five.** `comparative` and `processual` are claims
about how an article is written rather than about its numbers, so they have
no query yet and land with the diagram plan. `unclassified` is that gap
stated plainly rather than folded into `narrative`, which would report an
article carrying two figures as one carrying none.

chartable.description: Items whose numbers could have made a chart.
chartable.title: Chartable

chartable_charted.description: Of those, the ones a reader can see a rendered chart on.
chartable_charted.title: Chartable Charted

chartable_published.description: Chartable items that reached the day's published set. The denominator of the unused rate: an item that never published cannot carry a chart, and counting it would blame the planner for a fetch that failed.
chartable_published.title: Chartable Published

elements_found.description: Tier 1 elements the pass kept, added over the day. The extractor's own signal: it falls when the patterns stop matching, whatever the planner does.
elements_found.title: Elements Found

items.description: Planned items whose article carried text, so the pass ran on them. The denominator of the integrity rate, and never the published set.
items.title: Items

narrative.description: Items stating no quantity at all.
narrative.title: Narrative

span_integrity_pass.description: Of those, the ones where every element span cut its own characters.
span_integrity_pass.title: Span Integrity Pass

unclassified.description: Items with quantities but no unit shared widely enough.
unclassified.title: Unclassified

DayExtraction.title: DayExtraction

DayInstrument.description:
One measured eval-row column, aggregated over the day.

`column` names the eval-row column (an entry from `INSTRUMENT_COLUMNS`); the
reducer joins on it. `stat` carries the aggregate, additive and non-additive
parts kept apart by `DayDistribution`.
DayInstrument.title: DayInstrument

DayReasons.description:
Why each doubted item did not reach the top band.

Additive. A `high` item has no reason; every `medium` or `low` item falls
into exactly one bucket here, so the six counts partition the doubted set.
`unattributed` is a doubted item the checker recorded no reason for - a real
category the Model page counts separately, not the same fact as `not_scored`
(which is a recorded reason meaning no faithfulness score exists).

unattributed.description: Doubted, with no band_reason on the published item. Never source text.
unattributed.title: Unattributed

DayReasons.title: DayReasons

DaySource.description:
One source's day, counted so the reader can rank and combine without a re-walk.

Every count is additive within a source: sum a source's `published` over a
window for its window total. The reader combines days by keying on
`source_id`, then re-ranks - the ranking itself is non-additive, which is why
the whole per-source list is stored rather than a daily top list.

doubted.description: Of those, the ones not in the top band.
doubted.title: Doubted

published.description: Items this source contributed to the day.
published.title: Published

truncated.description: Of those, the ones extract cut at the cap.
truncated.title: Truncated

DaySource.title: DaySource

DayStageTiming.description:
One pipeline stage's wall-clock over the day's items.

`timed` and `sum_ms` are additive - a window's total stage time is the daily
totals added up, and a mean is `sum_ms` over `timed`. The three percentiles
are the day's own and are NOT additive: a median of daily medians is not the
window's median (the Model page's own caveat). A reader shows a daily
percentile or recomputes an exact one from a value population this record
does not carry. Empty percentiles are not zero: a stage that timed nothing
carries none of the four figures.

max_ms.description: The day's slowest item. Not additive.
max_ms.title: Max Ms

sum_ms.description: Every timed item added up. Additive.
sum_ms.title: Sum Ms

timed.description: Items that recorded milliseconds at this stage. Additive.
timed.title: Timed

DayStageTiming.title: DayStageTiming

DayThroughput.description:
The model's token clock for the day, so a rate survives without a runtime log.

Every field is additive: sum the milliseconds and the token counts over a
window and divide once for the window's prefill and decode rates. Reading the
prompt and writing the summary run at different rates, so their milliseconds
are kept apart. Null on the day facts when no item timed a token.

decode_ms.description: Milliseconds writing summaries, added over the day.
decode_ms.title: Decode Ms

items.description: Items that recorded any token count. The denominator.
items.title: Items

prefill_ms.description: Milliseconds reading prompts, added over the day.
prefill_ms.title: Prefill Ms

DayThroughput.title: DayThroughput

ItemStage.description: The terminal stage for an item.
ItemStage.title: ItemStage

changelog.why: Nothing said whether an article the planner drew nothing for had anything to draw, so a fall in published charts read the same whether the planner stopped choosing them or the extractor stopped finding numbers. The block is the day's join of the item-health census, which carries the class, against the published day, which carries the chart - both bounded by the day and neither by the archive (Guardrail #12). Nullable, because a record an earlier run wrote carries no such block and the console reads it leniently rather than dropping the whole day.

changelog.change: Initial shape: one record per published day, additive against non-additive.
changelog.why: The console rebuilt every per-day figure by walking the whole committed history on every build (research findings 61-75), a cost that rose with each published day for an answer that never changed once the day was frozen (Guardrail #12). This record carries those figures, written once by the producer that already holds the data. It stores a total only where a reader may add it across days and never as a running counter, because a correction to a counter needs a decrement path and a missed decrement is silent (owner, 2026-09-06); a correction rewrites this whole record instead. A non-additive figure carries the day's own value plus what a reader needs to combine days in a defined way (Andre).

description: Everything a run settled about one published day, for a later reducer to read.

addresses_considered.description: Distinct addresses the feeds offered the day, before what it had published or failed on (finding 62). Not additive - two days may repeat an address, so a reader treats a sum as an upper bound. Null on a day that recorded none.
addresses_considered.title: Addresses Considered

determinism_violations.description: Scored items whose identical inputs produced different words. Additive.
determinism_violations.title: Determinism Violations

extraction.description: What the candidate pass found and what the page drew from it, or null on a record written before 2026-09-08. Additive parts.

extraction_suspect.description: Scored items whose source read like page furniture. Additive.
extraction_suspect.title: Extraction Suspect

instruments.description: One entry per measured eval-row column (finding 74, note 38).
instruments.title: Instruments

items_failed.description: Planned items that never reached the digest. Additive.
items_failed.title: Items Failed

items_planned.description: Items the day's runs planned. Additive.
items_planned.title: Items Planned

items_published.description: Items in the day's published set. Additive.
items_published.title: Items Published

items_truncated.description: Published items extract cut at the truncation cap (finding 68). Additive.
items_truncated.title: Items Truncated

model_id.description: The model that wrote the day's summaries. Not additive - a per-day attribute a reader compares against the next day to find a model change (finding 70).
model_id.title: Model Id

pipeline_fingerprint.description: The digest of the declared settings the day ran under, as EvalRow carries it. Not additive - the boundary a model-change reading is drawn on (finding 70).
pipeline_fingerprint.title: Pipeline Fingerprint

revision.description: The ordinal of the newest run that published this day - DigestDay.runs[-1].n, the same number introduced_by_run counts up. A record whose revision is behind the day's own newest run is stale and must be rewritten (Fowler).
revision.title: Revision

runs.description: Runs that published this day. Additive.
runs.title: Runs

sources.description: One entry per source that published (findings 67, 68, 73).
sources.title: Sources

sources_present.description: Distinct sources that contributed a published item. Not additive - two days may share a source, so a reader combines the `sources` list rather than adding this across days. Equal to the length of `sources`.
sources_present.title: Sources Present

stage_timing.description: One entry per pipeline stage the day timed (findings 75, note 33).
stage_timing.title: Stage Timing

summaries_scored.description: Published items the checker gave a faithfulness score. Additive.
summaries_scored.title: Summaries Scored

throughput.description: The day's token clock, or null when no item timed a token. Additive parts.

visuals_rendered.description: Visuals that rendered on the day. Additive.
visuals_rendered.title: Visuals Rendered
